data.name: Aspenglen Campground
data.description: Aspenglen Campground is open for the summer! Campsites are available for tents and RVs. Campsites are available by reservation only. To make a reservation, visit www.recreation.gov online, use the Recreation.gov Mobile App or call 1-877-444-6777 and search for Rocky Mountain National Park - Aspenglen Campground.
data.audioDescription: Aspenglen Campground is open for the summer! Campsites are available for tents and RVs. Campsites are available by reservation only. To make a reservation, visit www.recreation.gov online, use the Recreation.gov Mobile App or call 1-877-444-6777 and search for Rocky Mountain National Park - Aspenglen Campground.
data.reservationInfo: During the summer camping season (late May-mid-Oct), all campsites are available by reservation only. Reservations can be made up to 6 months in advance of your desired camping date. To make a reservation, visit www.recreation.gov and search for Rocky Mountain National Park. Look for Aspenglen Campground.
data.regulationsOverview: There is an eight (8) person limit per site. Each camping site is limited to: one camping unit (i.e., a tent, RV, or trailer/tow vehicle) plus one additional tent. All tents shall be located on the tent pad. All additional camp structures must be self standing without impacts to vegetation or trees. Parking is limited to two (2) vehicles per site. A vehicle is defined as one vehicle, one trailer, one RV, or one towed unit. Each vehicle must be parked on the gravel or paved parking pad causing no resource degradation or encroachment onto the paved access road. Some sites will accommodate only one vehicle on the graveled parking pad. Extra vehicles must park in overflow areas. A timed entry reservation is included with your campground reservation. Campers can enter RMNP and check into the campground anytime after 1 p.m. For the protection of campers and wildlife, all food, pet food, cooking utensils and other scented items must be stored inside a provided food storage box or a locked vehicle.
data.directionsOverview: The road to Aspenglen Campground is located on the east side of Rocky Mountain National Park, just west of Fall River Entrance along U.S. Highway 34/Trail Ridge Road. If traveling from the Town of Estes Park, use U.S. Highway 34. If traveling from the west side of the park or from Beaver Meadows Entrance, at Deer Ridge Junction follow the signs toward Fall River Entrance and continue east past Horseshoe Park.

data.weatherOverview: Weather can vary greatly in Rocky Mountain National Park throughout the summer season. Be prepared for varying conditions. Expect sun, clouds, rain, or even snow. For the most up to date information on weather, visit https://www.weather.gov/bou/rmnp

accessibility.wheelchairAccess: There are two campsites available with raised fire grates and extended top picnic tables. When traveling around the campground, expect uneven compact natural soils on the surface of parking areas and walkways. Natural hazards like tree roots, gravel, sand and small rocks are found around the campground.
accessibility.internetInfo: WiFi service is not available at Aspenglen Campground.
accessibility.cellPhoneInfo: Depending on your service provider, cell phone service is not reliable at Aspenglen Campground.
accessibility.fireStovePolicy: Fires are only allowed in metal fire grates. Never leave fires or coals unattended. Fires must be completely extinguished before leaving campsite or going to bed. Gathering firewood or fire-starting materials is prohibited.
accessibility.rvInfo: Campsites are available for RVs and trailers up to 30 feet long. Aspenglen Campground does not have a dump station or fresh water fill available. Use Moraine Park or Glacier Basin Campgrounds to fill and empty tanks. There are no electric hookups. Generators may be used in Loop C. Generator use is permitted in the morning from 7:30 a.m. to 10 a.m. and in the evening from 4 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.
accessibility.additionalInfo: During the winter camping season, there is no water in Aspenglen Campground. Campers must bring their own water. Portable toilets are available. For your safety and the safety of wildlife, all food and scented items must be stored inside a food storage locker.
accessibility.adaInfo: There are two campsites available with raised fire grates and extended top picnic tables. When traveling around the campground, expect uneven compact natural soils on the surface of parking areas and walkways. Natural hazards like tree roots, gravel, sand and small rocks are found around the campground.

data.directionsOverview: Glacier Basin Campground is located approximately 5 miles up Bear Lake Road. The campground access road is located across from Park & Ride. If entering RMNP on U.S. Highway 36, enter the park via Beaver Meadows Entrance and take the first left-hand turn onto Bear Lake Road. If entering via the Grand Lake Entrance or Fall River Entrance, follow U.S. Highway 34 to Deer Ridge Junction and follow signs toward Beaver Meadows Entrance. Turn right up Bear Lake Road.

data.regulationsOverview: Check-in begins at 1 p.m. There is an eight (8) person limit per site. Each camping site is limited to: one camping unit (i.e., a tent, RV, or trailer/tow vehicle) plus one additional tent. All tents shall be located on the tent pad. All additional camp structures must be self standing without impacts to vegetation or trees. Parking is limited to two (2) vehicles per site. A vehicle is defined as one vehicle, one trailer, one RV, or one towed unit. Each vehicle must be parked on the gravel or paved parking pad causing no resource degradation or encroachment onto the paved access road. Some sites will accommodate only one vehicle on the graveled parking pad. Extra vehicles must park in overflow areas. Bears, Deer, elk, raccoons and skunks frequent the area: all food, pet food, cooking utensils and other scented items must be stored in a vehicle or food storage lockers located in the campground. For more regulations, visit https://www.nps.gov/romo/planyourvisit/camping.htm.

These sites have concrete parking pads with flat, concrete walking paths to a picnic table, fire ring, and tent pad area. data.name: Longs Peak Campground
data.description: Longs Peak Campground is closed for the 2026 season. If planning to camp inside RMNP, please check availability at Aspenglen, Timber Creek, or Moraine Park Campgrounds.
data.audioDescription: Longs Peak Campground is closed for the 2026 season. If planning to camp inside RMNP, please check availability at Aspenglen, Timber Creek, or Moraine Park Campgrounds.
data.reservationInfo: Longs Peak Campground is open from July to early September. Campsites are available on a first-come, first-served basis only. To pay for overnight camping fees at Longs Peak Campground, campers can use the Scan & Pay function on the Recreation.gov Mobile App. It is easy to pay using the Scan and Pay feature. First, download the Recreation.gov Mobile App and then create or update an account. Additional directions are posted at Longs Peak Campground.
data.regulationsOverview: Longs Peak Campground has 26 campsites for tents only. There is an eight (8) person limit per site. Each camping site is limited to: one camping unit (i.e., a tent) plus one additional tent. All tents shall be located on the tent pad. All additional camp structures must be self standing without impacts to vegetation or trees. Parking is limited to two (2) vehicles per site. A vehicle is defined as one vehicle, one trailer. Some campsites can only accommodate one vehicle on the designated graveled parking pad. Extra vehicles must park in overflow areas. Each vehicle must be parked on the gravel or paved parking pad causing no resource degradation or encroachment onto the paved access road. Wildlife including black bears, Mule deer and more frequent the area. All food items, scented items, pet food, cooking utensils, and coolers must be stored in a provided food storage box or inside a hard-sided vehicle. Lock your vehicle doors at all times. Bears can and will open vehicle doors to look for food rewards.

fees.description: The fee to camp at Longs Peak Campground is $30 per site, per night. There are no flushable toilets and campers need to bring their own drinkable water. To pay, download the Recreation.gov App and use the Scan & Pay feature - directions are available in the campground.

accessibility.wheelchairAccess: All campsites are designed for tents only. The surface around all campsites is uneven with rocks, branches, and other natural features. Some campsites have 3 to 6 steps to reach the tent pad.
accessibility.fireStovePolicy: Due to very high fire danger, Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are now in effect within Rocky Mountain National Park. This means that all campfires, including charcoal briquette fires are not permitted anywhere within Rocky Mountain National Park. This ban will remain in effect until further notice. Petroleum-fueled stoves and grills may still be used in developed campgrounds, picnic areas and in designated wilderness campsites. Stoves must be able to be turned on and off. When allowed, fires are only allowed in metal fire grates in campgrounds and picnic areas. Never leave fires or coals unattended. Fires must be completely extinguished before leaving campsite or going to bed. Gathering firewood or fire-starting materials is prohibited.
accessibility.rvInfo: Longs Peak Campground is a Tents Only campground
accessibility.additionalInfo: Timed Entry Reservations are required to enter all areas of Rocky Mountain National Park during certain times of the day. For most areas, they are required between the hours of 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. A timed entry is not included with the overnight camping fee for Longs Peak Campground.
